chains.title: ARID5B binding on ref T activates IRX3 and increases obesity risk

links.claim: Hypothesis: ref T binds ARID5B more strongly than alt C. ARID5B is the literature-nominated TF for this locus, but the supplied evidence has no ARID5B QBiC-SELEX model and no adipose/pre-adipocyte ARID5B ChIP peak at the variant (E19), so this allele-specific direction is not demonstrated.
The variant lies in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, consistent with a regulatory element.

If ARID5B positively regulates IRX3 in preadipocytes, ref T would raise IRX3; E17 reports only a pancreas IRX3 eQTL where alt C raises IRX3, E21 finds no subcutaneous adipose eQTL, and E02 gives only distance, so the adipose IRX3 link is unsupported and the required activator direction is not established.

The disease-relevant context is adipose/pre-adipocyte, but E04 has no ENCODE biosample matching that context and E19 finds no adipose ARID5B ChIP peak; absence is not definitive because the assay may be missing.

E15 reports T as the obesity/BMI effect allele, so this chain predicts T increases risk if ARID5B activation raises an obesogenic IRX3 signal; this matches the reported T effect direction but depends on the unsupported activator assumption.

chains.title: JUN repression on alt C lowers FTO and shifts risk toward ref T

links.claim: Hypothesis: alt C binds JUN more strongly than ref T. JUN is highly expressed in adipose and has a ChIP peak containing this variant only in HepG2, not adipose/pre-adipocytes (E05, E20), and no JUN QBiC-SELEX model is supplied, so allele-specific binding is unproven.
The variant lies in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, consistent with a regulatory element.

If JUN represses FTO in preadipocytes, alt C would lower FTO and ref T would leave FTO higher; E17 reports alt C raises FTO only in skeletal muscle, E21 finds no subcutaneous adipose eQTL, and E16 is L2G/fine-mapping evidence, so the adipose repression link is unsupported.
JUN is expressed in adipose (E05), but E04 and E20 show no matching adipose ENCODE ChIP peak at the variant, so occupancy in the proposed cell type is not established.

E15 reports T as the obesity/BMI effect allele; this chain predicts T risk if higher FTO is obesogenic and alt C lowers FTO through JUN repression, but the adipose FTO repression direction is not supported by the supplied data.

predictions: JUN binding is stronger on alt C than ref T in preadipocytes
Alt C lowers FTO in preadipocytes if JUN represses FTO
T is the obesity-increasing allele because ref T has less JUN-mediated FTO repression
falsified_if: JUN binding is not stronger on alt C than ref T in preadipocytes
JUN perturbation does not alter FTO in preadipocytes

grades_v0.reason: No ARID5B ChIP peak over the variant in adipose/pre-adipocytes and no ARID5B QBiC-SELEX model/change is provided. The claim itself states the direction is unsupported.
E03 directly places the variant in EH38E3181208, a dELS distal enhancer-like cCRE; E04 confirms the same cCRE class.
E17 reports an IRX3 eQTL in pancreas, not adipose, and E02 only gives distance. No evidence shows ARID5B regulates IRX3 or that the effect is adipocyte-specific.
E04 explicitly states no ENCODE biosample matches the adipose expression context, supporting the claim that matching adipose ChIP data are absent.
E15 reports T as the effect allele for obesity/BMI, whereas this chain predicts alt C as the obesity-increasing allele. The association is strong, but the direction contradicts the chain.

E05 provides only a JUN ChIP peak in HepG2, not adipose/pre-adipocytes, and no JUN QBiC-SELEX change is supplied. Neither required occupancy in the relevant cell type nor an allele-specific binding assay supports the claim.
E03 and E04 support the variant lying in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE.

E17 supports higher FTO expression for alt C only in skeletal muscle, not adipose, and E16 is L2G/fine-mapping evidence. No JUN perturbation or adipocyte allele-specific reporter shows JUN regulates FTO.
E05 supports JUN expression in adipose (442.88 TPM, rank 3), and E04/E05 support that no matching adipose ENCODE ChIP exists in the supplied data.
E15 reports T as the obesity/BMI effect allele, while this chain predicts alt C increases risk through FTO. The direction is inconsistent with the chain.
E11 provides only an SP1 ChIP peak in HCT116, not adipose/pre-adipocytes, and no SP1 QBiC-SELEX change is supplied. Allele-specific binding in the relevant cell type is unproven.
E03 and E04 support the variant lying in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE.
E17 supports higher FTO expression for alt C in skeletal muscle, not adipose, and E16 is L2G evidence. No SP1 perturbation or adipocyte assay connects SP1 to FTO.
E11 supports SP1 expression in adipose (41.01 TPM, rank 145), and E04/E11 support that no matching adipose ENCODE ChIP exists in the supplied data.
E15 reports T as the obesity/BMI effect allele, while this chain predicts alt C increases risk through FTO. The direction is inconsistent with the chain.

grades_final.reason: No ARID5B QBiC-SELEX model is supplied, and E19 only reports absence of an adipose ARID5B ChIP peak at the variant, with the caveat that the assay may not exist. No allele-specific ARID5B binding in preadipocytes or direction ref T > alt C is demonstrated.
E03 places the variant in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, and E04 confirms the cCRE class as dELS.

E02 provides only distance to IRX3. E17 reports an IRX3 eQTL in pancreas where alt C raises IRX3, not an adipose/pre-adipocyte ARID5B-dependent effect, and E21 finds no subcutaneous adipose eQTL. The required ref-T/ARID5B activation of IRX3 is not established.

E04 and E19 show no ENCODE biosample matching adipose/pre-adipocyte and no adipose ARID5B ChIP peak at the variant. Absence is not definitive, but there is no positive evidence for ARID5B relevance or occupancy in the proposed cell type.

E15 supports T as an obesity/BMI-increasing allele, and E16 supports credible-set/L2G evidence at FTO. This supports the phenotype association and T direction, but not the chain-specific ARID5B–IRX3 mechanism; the phenotype link remains conditional on missing upstream links.

E05/E20 show JUN is highly expressed in adipose and has a ChIP peak containing the variant only in HepG2, not adipose/pre-adipocytes. No JUN QBiC-SELEX model or adipose allele-specific occupancy is provided, so alt C > ref T binding is indirect and unproven.
E03 places the variant in EH38E3181208, a distal enhancer-like cCRE, and E04 confirms the cCRE class as dELS.

E17 reports an FTO eQTL in skeletal muscle where alt C raises FTO, opposite to the proposed alt-C JUN repression lowering FTO. E21 finds no subcutaneous adipose eQTL, and E16 is fine-mapping/L2G evidence, not evidence that JUN represses FTO in preadipocytes.

E05 supports JUN expression in adipose, but E04 and E20 show no matching adipose ENCODE ChIP peak at the variant. Expression in the relevant tissue is present, but occupancy/activity at this element in preadipocytes is not established.

E15 supports T as an obesity/BMI-increasing allele, and E16 supports association/credible-set evidence. However, the chain requires alt C to lower FTO through JUN repression, which is not supported and is opposite to the supplied skeletal-muscle FTO eQTL direction; only the T-risk association is consistent.

checks.why: Would directly test the highest-probability chain by asking whether ARID5B occupies this variant in adipose; absence would strongly weaken ARID5B_ref.
Would test whether JUN, a highly expressed adipose TF, actually occupies the variant in adipose rather than only in HepG2.
Would test the tissue-relevant gene link for FTO; a null adipose eQTL would weaken both JUN_alt and SP1_alt gene claims and support the null/context-mismatch concern.
